approachQuestion.prompt: A row of sculptures has pairwise distinct positive integer heights. Two sculptures at positions i < j can see one another exactly when every height strictly between them is smaller than both endpoint heights; adjacent sculptures always see one another. Return the number of unordered visible pairs. Example: [7, 2, 5, 3] returns 4: positions (0,1), (0,2), (1,2), and (2,3). Choose the best approach.
constraints: The input is immutable; n is between 1 and 200,000. All integers, indices, counts, and arithmetic results fit in signed 64-bit machine words; comparisons and arithmetic have unit cost.
Input and returned output are excluded from auxiliary space. Working stacks, arrays, and copies count. No hashing is used.

options.text: Scan left to right with a decreasing stack of heights. Pop each height smaller than the current height, adding one pair per pop. If the stack is still nonempty, add one more pair. Push the current height.
options.feedback: Each popped top sees the current sculpture; previously popped heights are lower than it. The first surviving taller sculpture also sees the current one and blocks every earlier survivor.

options.text: Use a decreasing stack, counting one pair per popped smaller height, but count no pair when a taller top remains.
options.feedback: A taller neighbor is still visible. For [5, 2], nothing pops and this returns 0 instead of 1.

options.text: Pop smaller heights, count each pop, and also count a pair with every surviving stack height.
options.feedback: The nearest surviving taller height blocks earlier survivors. For [7, 5, 2], only the two adjacent pairs are visible, not the endpoint pair.

options.text: For each endpoint pair scan every intermediate height and test the visibility definition.
options.feedback: The result is correct, but repeatedly scanning interiors for all endpoint pairs is clearly inefficient. One scan can settle pairs as blocking candidates disappear.

feedback.reason: Count all newly exposed pairs during candidate removal, and include the first surviving blocker.
details: Keep heights in decreasing order. A new height forms one pair with every smaller top removed, plus one pair with the first taller top that remains. Add the new height afterward. Do not enumerate pairs with earlier surviving heights.

A new taller sculpture sees each shorter top it removes, then only the nearest taller blocker left. Earlier taller survivors are hidden by that blocker. Distinct heights avoid needing multiplicity groups.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For count-pops-and-blocker, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the number of sculptures. Keep only a scalar count and the height stack. The output is one scalar and no pairs are materialized.
constraints: Stack push, pop, and top take amortized constant time using a growable array; each entry uses a constant number of words. Count the working stack, but exclude input and final output. No recursive call stack or hash table is used.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: One push/pop per sculpture bounds all visibility checks together.
details: There is one push per sculpture, at most one pop per sculpture, and at most one surviving-blocker check per iteration. Total time is linear. A decreasing row retains n heights, so auxiliary space is linear.
